{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂er-}}

# {{lb|en|obsolete}} A precise point in time; a moment.

I ſet out all his rotes and '''tenſes'''{{...}}}} # {{senseid|en|grammatical aspect}} {{lb|en|grammar|countable|proscribed}} A grammatical {{m|en|aspect|id=grammatical quality of a verb}}. # {{senseid|en|grammar}} {{lb|en|grammar|countable|proscribed}} A verb form or construction indicating a combination of {{m|en|tense|id=property indicating a point in time}}, {{m|en|aspect|id=grammatical quality of a verb}}, and {{m|en|mood|id=grammatical}}. #: {{ux|en|The "simple present" '''tense''' in English can have several meanings.}} #:: Habits: I '''walk''' my dog every day. #:: Stative verbs: You '''are''' happy. #:: Facts: The Earth '''revolves''' around the Sun. #:: Etc. #: {{ux|en|The Spanish teacher told the student to use the imperfect '''tense''' instead of the preterite '''tense'''.}} =====Usage notes===== * Some English-language authorities only consider inflected forms of verbs (i.e. the present and past tenses) as tenses, and not periphrastic forms such as the simple future with {{m|en|will}}. * Grammatically tense (the location of an event in time: past, present, future) is often distinguished from {{m|en|aspect|id=grammatical quality of a verb}} (how an event occurs or is viewed by the speaker: finished, ongoing, habitual, etc.). So ''I am eating'' and ''I was eating'' have different tenses (present and past) but the same aspect (continuous), whereas ''I was eating'' and ''I had eaten'' have the same tense (past) and different aspects (continuous and perfect).
